name: Testing Specialized Reasoning and Knowledge
gist: Papers create benchmarks for narrow domains like medical diagnosis, chemistry, law, theorem proving, or biological science — where background knowledge and careful reasoning both matter.
explain: Some domains require not just general intelligence but deep background knowledge and precise reasoning. You cannot diagnose a rare disease without understanding medicine. You cannot prove a theorem without logic. You cannot synthesize a stable drug without chemistry. This subtheme is about building benchmarks for these specialized domains where models have to show they actually understand the field, not just pattern-match.

The challenge is that general-purpose benchmarks miss domain-specific nuance. A medical benchmark cannot just ask "which drug treats this disease?" because context matters enormously: the patient's age, allergies, other medications, kidney function, pregnancy status. A chemistry benchmark cannot just ask "does this molecule exist?" because stability and synthesis routes matter. A law benchmark cannot just ask "is this legal?" because precedent and jurisdiction and interpretation matter. Building benchmarks for these fields requires collaboration with experts who understand what real reasoning looks like in that domain.

The papers here tackle narrow domains: medical diagnosis, chemistry and molecular design, law and legal reasoning, theorem proving in formal mathematics, biological sciences. Each team builds tests that capture what it means to truly understand that field. Some use real examples from practice: actual medical cases, actual legal documents, actual chemistry papers. Others create synthetic tests carefully designed by domain experts to probe specific understanding. The goal is to move past generic benchmarks toward specialized evaluation that honors the actual difficulty and knowledge required in each field.

papers.title: CAPSUL: A Comprehensive Human Protein Benchmark for Subcellular Localization
papers.contribution: Demonstrates importance of structural features through evaluation of state-of-the-art models and discovers a decisive alpha-helix localization pattern through interpretable attention mechanisms.

papers.title: FormalML: A Benchmark for Evaluating Formal Subgoal Completion in Machine Learning Theory
papers.contribution: State-of-the-art provers highlight persistent limitations in accuracy and efficiency on this first benchmark combining premise retrieval with complex research-level contexts.

papers.title: ProfBench: Multi-Domain Rubrics requiring Professional Knowledge to Answer and Judge
papers.contribution: Reveals GPT-5-high achieves only 65.9% overall performance on professional-domain tasks and identifies notable disparities between proprietary and open-weight models.

papers.title: SorryDB: Can AI Provers Complete Real-World Lean Theorems?
papers.contribution: Continuously updated stream of 1000+ real formalization tasks showing complementary strengths across approaches and reducing test contamination.

papers.title: VenusX: Unlocking Fine-Grained Functional Understanding of Proteins
papers.contribution: Comprehensive evaluation of diverse models (protein language models, sequence-structure hybrids, structure-based, alignment-based) reveals performance gaps across in-distribution and out-of-distribution scenarios.

papers.title: 3DCS: Datasets and Benchmark for Evaluating Conformational Sensitivity in Molecular Representations
papers.contribution: Reveals that modern data-driven representations handle geometry well but inconsistently handle chirality and poorly align with energy landscapes, providing the first rigorous benchmark for 3D molecular representations.

papers.title: AbdCTBench: Learning Clinical Biomarker Representations from Abdominal Surface Geometry
papers.contribution: Demonstrates surface geometry is predictive of internal tissue composition; best models achieve age prediction MAE 6.22 years (R²=0.757), mortality AUROC 0.839, diabetes detection AUROC 0.801.

papers.title: Can You Hear Me Now? A Benchmark for Long-Range Graph Propagation
papers.contribution: Benchmarking reveals clear performance gaps in long-range propagation, establishing ECHO as a new standard for evaluating long-range information propagation in GNNs.

papers.title: GeomMotif: A Benchmark for Arbitrary Geometric Preservation in Protein Generation
papers.contribution: Reveals sequence-based and structure-based models find different tasks challenging, with geometric preservation varying significantly by structural context.

papers.title: MolLangBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Language-Prompted Molecular Structure Recognition, Editing, and Generation
papers.contribution: Shows strongest model (GPT-5) achieves only 86.2% and 85.5% on recognition and editing, and 43.0% on generation, revealing significant limitations in molecular manipulation.

papers.title: ProtDBench: A Unified Benchmark of Protein Binder Design and Evaluation
papers.contribution: Reveals substantial verifier-dependent bias in structure prediction, systematic differences between filtering rules and success definitions, providing fair reproducible evaluation for protein design.

papers.title: SEDRAS: Symbolically Evaluated Deep Research And Science
papers.contribution: Produces 600 diverse evaluation scenarios revealing that different models excel at different tasks, with Gemini 3.0 Pro achieving best overall score but GPT 5.2 strongest on symbolic data, Claude Opus 4.5 on files, and Grok 4.1 when complexity scales.

papers.title: TadA-Bench: A Million-Variant Benchmark for Future-Round Discovery Toward Agentic Protein Engineering
papers.contribution: Shows strong interpolation but weaker future-round ranking; positions TadA-Bench as reproducible wet-lab substrate; demonstrates evolutionary coverage is more informative than local data density.
